factsheet.heading: UNIVERSITY OF WESTMINSTER: NCS and Tower Tavern
paragraphs: The University of Westminster's New Cavendish Street campus is one of London's significant post-war educational buildings. Designed by Lyons, Israel and Ellis and opened in 1971 alongside the designation of the Polytechnic of Central London, it represents an important moment in the evolution of higher education and the architecture of the modern polytechnic.

This Open House weekend invites visitors to explore the campus through its architecture, history and contemporary role within Fitzrovia. Guided walks will introduce the building's design, planning and changing relationship with the surrounding neighbourhood, while interpretation boards throughout the campus will reveal stories from its past and present.

The programme concludes in the University's Tower Tavern, a former public house now being reimagined as a Centre for Interdisciplinary Exchange, for an evening reception and talk, Pints and the Poly. Together we will explore the intertwined histories of Westminster, the Polytechnic movement and Fitzrovia, reflecting on how educational institutions continue to shape civic life and public space.
Visitors will be guided through the New Cavendish Street campus with tours, and interpretation boards highlighting the building's architecture, development and historical significance.

Three guided tours will take place on Saturday 19th September: two shorter morning tours focusing on the building, and a longer afternoon Walk & Talk exploring the campus, its architecture and its relationship with Fitzrovia.

From 5.00pm, visitors are invited to the Tower Tavern for an informal drinks reception followed by Pints and the Poly, an illustrated talk exploring the history of the University of Westminster, the wider Polytechnic movement and the changing social and urban history of Fitzrovia.
